notes: PREDICTED, before the run, from the RUNBOOK family rule that this gate answer is set by the failure class and not by the site: 1,857,893 of 5,252,000 across 147 of 351 channels, all 27 scenarios alive -- the number ParseInAry_Opt and ParseInput_Dbl_Opt both measured for the same edit.

THE PREDICTION IS FALSIFIED, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. An INTEGER control parameter is a MODE, not a gain. Adding one to every value this unit parses selects a different controller path in every scenario, and most of them then produce no comparable output at all: 728,000 values compared against 5,252,000 in the green run, with mismatches in scenarios 19, 20 and 27 only. This is a THIRD failure class beside the two the RUNBOOK records (every parsed value wrong -> 1,857,893 / 5,252,000 / 147 ch; the parse fails -> 1,583,216 / 4,732,000 / 131 ch), and it says the family rule is about the failure class and NOT about the item type -- which is exactly the reading the prediction was written to be able to refute.
The red test still does what a red test must: the perturbation moved 370,646 values and the revert moved 0 of 5,252,000.
